Navy, cream, Amboqia, and Geist hold, the caption honestly explains the bars, and the figures look sourced, but the fold is one repeating row with no jump, no opened control, and no reason to keep scrolling. Put the actual Command demo in the header so a visitor can type or jump, and make every row share one photographic treatment instead of mixing listing thumbs with navy letter tiles.

defects.section: Mobile Bend row, Jax badge overlay
defects.finding: On mobile the circular Jax mascot badge sits directly on top of the Bend row's count label, clipping "13 for lease" down to "13 f" — the figure is unreadable at 375px.

The bars are flat single-tone fills with no hover/tap affordance visible anywhere in either shot — no cursor state, no tooltip trigger, no expand control. As drawn this is a static ranked-bar illustration, not an interactive data section; nothing here promises a hover reveals more (e.g. the underlying lease list, a rate distribution, or a map pin) the way the criterion requires.

Every row repeats the identical shape (label, sourced rate sentence, gray bar, bold count) with no differentiation by rate tier, no color coding, no map context, and no photographic anchor — correct per the house-ledger layout lock, but undifferentiated enough that reading the first row tells you the whole page.

rows.dullest: The town ledger bars themselves — flat navy/gray fills sorted by count, each row identical in structure to the last, with no color tiering, sparkline, map, or photo. Once you've read the Bend row you've read the whole page.
rows.beats: LoopNet's Bend commercial-lease search results — this page wins on immediate town-level rate transparency (a sourced per-sq-ft range and count for every Central Oregon town visible without filtering), but loses on live inventory depth, photos, and per-listing detail, which are the metrics that actually matter to a tenant.
rows.verdict: This is a correctly-branded, correctly-sourced town ledger that satisfies the layout lock's letter (H1 ledger, length-encoded counts, sourced rate lines under each name) but not its ambition — demoMatch is false because no catalog interaction (Avatar, Button, Sheet, Carousel, morphing search) appears anywhere in the shots; this is a house form only. No named TASTE.md tell fires outright since the bar is a real visual mark, but the page is still a flat, static ranked list with a mobile clipping defect (the Jax badge eating the Bend count) and zero visible interaction affordance across six identical rows.
